taxonomyNote: The Oregon assessment notes the A. flavipunctatus complex may comprise several species (e.g. the Santa Cruz form A. f. niger and the Shasta lineage); NatureServe treats it as one species, Speckled Black Salamander.
fieldMarks: Adults slate to black above and below, often with small white spots or a wash of bronze or olive.
Up to about 94 mm snout-vent and 160 mm total length; 15-16 costal grooves; short limbs.
Larger adults have a triangular head from large jaw muscles; toe tips are not squared, unlike its congeners.
Juveniles are green-grey or brassy with yellow limb bases and small white or blue spots; in the far north adults keep the juvenile greenish-grey or brassy look.
behavior: Terrestrial and needs no standing water for any life stage; eggs are laid underground in July-August and hatch as miniature adults.
Active on the surface year-round in moist places and the south, but retreats underground in dry summers in drier northern sites; active mainly October-April in the north.
Aggressive, with bite-hold behaviour; 35% of field-caught animals were scarred. Good jumper using its tail.
Eats terrestrial arthropods, snails and worms.
habitat: Forest, woodland and grassland; southern populations prefer moist woodland along streams and seepages, northern populations grassy areas, and far-north populations moss-covered rockslides.
Found under surface cover such as rocks, logs and talus near creeks or seeps.
range: Southwestern Oregon south through the California coastal mountains to the Russian River (Sonoma County), with isolated populations near Santa Cruz and around Shasta Lake; sea level to about 1,700 m. Not found in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Clouded salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Clouded salamander has squared toe tips and brassy specks on a brown, often lighter back; black salamander toe tips are not squared and adults are slate to black.

aliases: Santa Cruz black salamander (A. f. niger)
